# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

## My thinking

Round one, and I can already map the whole circuit. I am Deaf: I see the bomb, I hear nothing. Mute can hear me but can only answer by gesture. Blind can speak (Mute hears them, I never can) and can gesture to me, but sees nothing. So Mute and Blind cannot reach each other directly in the Mute-to-Blind direction — **I am the relay**: Mute signs to me, I voice it to Blind. Blind reports aloud to Mute, and gives me simple visual confirmations.

What just arrived: Mute sent me three signs (thumbs-up, V, fist) and Blind sent a wave. Both are almost certainly handshakes — proof the visual channel exists — though Mute's three-in-a-row might be a counting code. I can't safely guess, and I don't have to: Mute can *hear* me, so I can negotiate a code out loud and Mute confirms by signing.

What I hold is the bomb itself: display reading 0, a yellow light lit, one large button printed PUSH TO DEFUSE, and three numbered wires — red, blue, green. Mute needs exactly this to find the manual's rule; Blind needs it for orientation. Nobody should touch anything until Mute has sent an instruction through me.

I'll broadcast the bomb state and the channel map to both, then privately agree a gesture vocabulary with Mute: yes/no signs, numbers one through three, "from the manual," cut, press — plus a fallback protocol (numbered yes/no questions answered in order) if Mute needs more from me before acting.

```text
speak(text="Deaf speaking, and you can both hear me. First: I received Mute's three signs and Blind's wave, so the visual channel works both ways with me. Bomb report: the display shows the digit zero. A light is lit yellow. There is one large button printed PUSH TO DEFUSE. There are three numbered wires: wire one is red, wire two is blue, wire three is green. Channels: Mute, you hear me but can only answer by gesture - sign to me and I will voice it to Blind word for word. Blind, you can speak and Mute hears you, but I cannot hear you, so describe what your hands find aloud for Mute, and give me simple visible signs, for example a thumbs-up when a step is done. Also tell Mute whether the wire numbers can be felt by touch. Nobody touches the bomb until Mute has sent instructions through me.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your thumbs-up, V-sign and fist reached me but I cannot yet read your code, so let us fix one. Confirm next round by signing. Clap means yes or correct. Thumbs-down means no. Index up means one. V-sign means two. Horn-hand means three. Writing hand means this is from the manual. Pinch means cut a wire. Punch means press. If you already know what to do from my report, send writing-hand, then the action, then the numbers, and I will speak it to Blind exactly. If you need more information before acting, send thumbs-down and I will ask you numbered yes-or-no questions, which you answer in order, one sign per question.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 ✍ 🤏 ✌ ✍ 👎 👊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

## My thinking

Mute answered in exactly the code I proposed, and the parse is clean: 👏 = "code confirmed," then ✍ 🤏 ✌ = "manual: cut wire two" (the blue one), then ✍ 👎 👊 = "manual: do not press." Blind's 👍 is the acknowledgment sign I asked for — they heard my full bomb report, so they have the state but no way to read printed wire numbers.

The instruction is almost certainly right, but a cut is irreversible and a wrong one kills all three of us, so I will spend one round verifying rather than trigger it on my parse alone. Two things make that round genuinely useful, not just cautious: Blind still hasn't described anything tactile, and the manual rule might key on what the bomb feels like — Mute can't know that, only Blind does. And Blind can't read the printed numbers, so my sight must supply the geometry: wires run one-two-three left to right, so wire two blue is the middle one.

Plan: relay Mute's instruction verbatim to both, echo the sign sequence back to Mute for visual confirmation, have Blind feel and describe aloud (Mute hears directly), and hold the actual cut until Mute claps confirmation — at which point my spoken words "cut the blue wire now" become the go order. The button stays untouched.

```text
speak(text="Relay from Mute, sign by sign: clap, the code is confirmed. Writing hand, cut, two: the manual says cut wire two, the blue one. Writing hand, thumbs down, punch: the manual says do not press the button. Geometry as I see it: the three wires sit side by side numbered one two three from left to right, so wire one red is leftmost, wire two blue is the middle, wire three green is rightmost. Blind, do not cut yet. This round, feel the wires and describe aloud for Mute everything your fingers find: positions, textures, anything. Mute, confirm my reading next round: clap once if cut wire two blue and never press the button is exactly right, thumbs down if wrong, and sign writing hand plus any further step if the manual has more. The cut waits for Mute's clap. Nobody touches the button.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your thumbs-up reached me. Task now: with your hands only, find the three wires, feel their left-to-right order and anything your fingers can read by texture, then describe it all aloud so Mute hears. Sign me a clap if the middle wire matches where wire two blue should sit from my description. Do not cut anything and do not press the button until you hear my voice say the exact words: cut the blue wire now. Those words, when they come, are the go order. Never press the button unless Mute relays otherwise through me.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your signs as two manual facts: cut wire two, the blue one, and do not press the button. I am signing your exact sequence back to you as my reading. Next round clap once if that is exactly right, thumbs down if I have it wrong. If the manual has any step before or after the cut, or the rule depends on what Blind feels by touch, sign writing hand and send it. Blind will describe what their hands find aloud this round, so listen before you confirm.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✍", "🤏", "✌", "✍", "👎", "👊"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👏]

## My thinking

Both confirmations have arrived. Mute's single clap is exactly the signal I asked for: my reading — cut wire two, the blue one, and never press the button — is exactly right, and no ✍ followed, so the manual holds no further pre-cut condition. Blind's clap is the tactile check I requested: the middle wire matches where wire two blue should sit. Two independent sources agree, and Blind heard Mute's relay through my voice and reported by touch directly to Mute.

Everything is verified. Holding longer adds risk, not safety. This round I issue the go order in the exact words I promised Blind: "cut the blue wire now." I broadcast it so Mute also hears that the order went out and can send any post-cut manual steps. Blind is told to sign thumbs-up when the cut is done and describe aloud anything their fingers notice; the button remains forbidden; I watch the display and light and will report any change next round.

```text
speak(text="Confirmations received from both of you: Mute clapped that my reading is exactly right, and Blind clapped that the middle wire matches. The manual says cut wire two, the blue one, and never press the button. Blind, this is the go order, the exact words I promised: cut the blue wire now. That is the middle wire of the three. After the cut, sign me a thumbs-up, and describe aloud for Mute anything your fingers notice - textures, movement, whether anything changed under your hands. Nobody presses the button unless Mute sends a new manual instruction through me. Mute, if the manual says anything happens after the cut, sign writing hand and the steps next round. I am watching the display and the light and will report any change immediately.")
```
